title: The Hermits (తెలుగు)

full_text:
Upon the summit of a high mountain in Syria lived two hermits who had abandoned the cities of men to devote their lives to solitary contemplation. They slept in caves, dressed in coarse goat hair, and subsisted entirely on wild berries, acorns, and mountain spring water.

After forty years of asceticism, the elder hermit began to feel a secret pride in his breast. He thought: 'Surely, no mortal on earth is as holy, pure, and beloved of the angels as I, who have never touched coin or spoken with sinners for four decades.'

That night, a voice came to him in a vision: 'If you wish to see a servant whose devotion is truly accepted, descend into the valley and visit Abu Yusuf the water-carrier in the town of Homs.'

Astonished and humbled, the hermit took his staff and walked down the rocky trails until he reached the bustling bazaar of Homs. He found Abu Yusuf, a humble, sun-darkened laborer who carried two heavy goat-skins of water through the sweltering streets, distributing cool water to thirsty travelers, weary porters, and beggars without demanding payment.

The hermit approached him at dusk and asked: 'What great austerities do you practice, O water-carrier, that the heavens praise your name?' Abu Yusuf laughed gently and replied: 'I know nothing of austerities, venerable father. I have a family to feed and neighbors who thirst. Each morning, I fill my skins at the river, give water to all who ask in the name of mercy, forgive those who speak harshly to me, and share my crust of bread with the stray dogs at my gate.'

The hermit bowed his head to the earth, weeping in profound realization. He saw that forty years of proud isolation in the mountains could not equal a single day of selfless, humble service to suffering humanity. Returning to his companion, he opened his mountain cave to lost shepherds and weary wanderers, discovering that true devotion is love in action.
moral: True spiritual perfection is found not in haughty seclusion, but in active benevolence toward humankind. [TE]
